scenario: [LDTL.4.1]: `retain:` demands a value, so it is a concrete-value position ([LNUL.5.1]), and the compiler must refuse an un-narrowed `Duration?` there with DS_VALIDATE_NULLABLE_UNNARROWED. `Trig.d` is `Duration?` and nothing narrows it: narrowing stops at the arrow ([LNUL.5.2]), and the rule has no `where`. The type is right, so this is not the TYPE_MISMATCH of LDTL.4.1_retain_not_duration_rejects; LDTL.4.1_retain_with_dynamic_ttl_ok is the control that compiles. A compiler that typed the leaf but ignored nullability compiles this one. PATH PINNED: `dsc.validate.ldtl_3_2_retain`, through `dsc.typecheck.lnul_5_1_concrete`.
rules_ds:
use default:
    dynamic_ttl: true

schema Trig scope logical:
    k: Int key
    d: Duration? mutable
schema Reading scope ttl 30_s:
    k: Int
    v: Int

rule r:
    Trig t
->
    emit Reading k: t.k v: 1 retain: t.d
